title: Price vs. quantity in oligopoly games
summary_en: Cournot (quantity) and Bertrand (price) competition give different oligopoly outcomes — but how do firms choose which to use? Tasnádi studies oligopolists who can commit to either a price or a quantity strategy and characterises the equilibrium choice as a function of demand curvature, capacity costs, and strategic substitutability. The paper resolves a long-standing question in industrial-organisation theory by identifying the parameter conditions under which firms endogenously prefer Cournot vs. Bertrand competition.
data_used: Theoretical paper in industrial organisation. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Theoretical input for Hungarian competition-policy analysis (GVH merger reviews, MEKH market-structure assessments): the choice between price- and quantity-competition modelling assumptions matters for predicted equilibrium concentration and welfare in concentrated markets — Hungarian mobile telecommunications, retail energy, supermarket retail. The paper provides the analytical lens for picking the right competition mode based on observable market features.
